sentences.text: Fuel planning uses the rule of thirds: plan to use one third of your fuel going out, one third coming back, and keep one third in reserve.
Say your spot is forty-two miles out, you cruise at fourteen knots, and you burn eighteen gallons an hour.
The run out takes three hours and uses fifty-four gallons.
By the rule of thirds, you need three times fifty-four, or one hundred sixty-two gallons aboard.
Rough seas, head winds and heavy loads all burn more fuel, so be conservative.
